newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria elects Svetoslav Gavriiski to head c.bank. [CORRECTED 11:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria elects Svetoslav Gavriiski to head c.bank. [CORRECTED 11:30 GMT]

text.p: Bulgaria's parliament on Wednesday elected Svetoslav Gavriiski as a governor of the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) to operate under a currency board system to be launched on July 1 to stabilise the economy.
Of 214 deputies (corrects number of deputies) present in the 240-seat chamber 186 voted for Gavriiski, six opposed his nomination and 22 abstained.

Gavriiski, 49, a deputy finance minister, will succeed current governor Lyubomir Filipov and head the BNB under an IMF-prescribed currency board system designed to stabilise the fragile local currency, the lev, and the country's shaky banks.
"I hope we will be able to solve the serious problems of financial stabilisation and we rely on your support," Gavriiski told parliament after the vote.
Gavriiski served as Finance Minister in a three-month interim cabinet appointed in February after mass protests ousted a Socialist government for leading the country into a grave economic crisis.

He asked parliament to give him one or two days more for consultations before proposing nominations for three deputy governors to head the three BNB departments that will play a key role under the currency board system.

"I would like that the nominations were supported by all political forces. There will be no members of the current (BNB) board among them... because the new policy should be implemented by new people with a new way of thinking," Gavriiski told reporters.

The Issue Department implements the currency board, overseeing that levs in circulation are fully matched by foreign exchange reserves estimated at around $1 billion at the time of introduction and never provides credit to any account holder.
The Banking Department manages the lender of last resort role and reserve requirements for commercial banks with the aim of ensuring the functioning of financial markets.

The currency board system bans central bank lending to the government and commercial banks, but the law allows the banking department to lend up to a three-month lev credit to a solvent commercial bank in case of systemic risk only against gold or hard currency collateral.
The third department, the Bank Supervision Department, enforces prudential regulations and banking laws to ensure soundness of the banking system.

Gavriiski said he would seek immediate technical advice from the IMF on the separation of the assets and liabilities of the Issue Department and the Banking Department prior to the introduction of the currency board.
The remaining three members of the seven-member BNB board are to be appointed by the president.
Parliament has yet to pass this year's budget and a Banking Law to complete preparations for launching the currency board. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
